digest.component_or_area: git-backed tickets store / compaction and sync recovery
propositions: Parallel multi-session writes to the shared git-backed tickets store cause chronic wedging due to unrolled compaction mutations (SNAPSHOT write, *.retired renames, .archived deletions) that occur before git commit, leaving dirty worktree on worker death.

The sync merge operation (_union_merge) aborts on two variants of dirty state: untracked files that origin wants to create, and tracked-file deletions/modifications that would be overwritten, stranding local ticket commits and breaking plan-review/close attestation.
Runtime markers (*/.archived and */.write.lock) are tracked in HEAD despite gitignore patterns, causing routine marker churn to appear as persistent tracked dirt that blocks merge and status checks.

Compaction fold must achieve crash-atomicity via intent journal (commit-pending sentinel outside worktree) with recovery preamble that reverts abandoned partial folds under write lock, ensuring dirty state is never produced.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must default to active-ticket scope to track working-set cost as store grows, with --include-archived override to reach archived tickets.
